# Class 4 {.ct}

![](../graphics/REB_Logo.png){fig-alt="Reaction Engineering Basics Logo" fig-align="center" width="200"}

## The Bodenstein Steady-State Approximation {.cc}

Class 4 examines the use of the Bodenstein steady-state approximation for generating mechanistic rate expressions. It explains the relationship between the rate of mechanistic steps and the apparent rate of non-elementary reactions. Apparent rate coefficients and limiting forms of rate expressions are introduced.

## Learning Outcomes {.ch}

After completing Class 4 you should...

* Know
    * the definition of a reactive intermediate, kinetically insignificant step, effectively irreversible step, apparent rate coefficient, and limiting form of a rate expression
    * the defining equations for the net rate of generation of a species in terms of the rates of mechanistic steps, and the Bodenstein steady-state approximation
* Understand
    * mechanistic steps are elementary reactions
    * there must be a linear combination of the mechanistic steps that equals the apparent, non-elementary reaction
    * mechanistic steps must be reversible, but the reverse rate may be negligibly small
* Be able to
    * write an expression for the rate of generation of a reactant or product of a non-elementary reaction in terms of its rates of generation in the steps of the reaction’s mechanism
    * simplify rate expressions for kinetically insignificant and effectively irreversible steps
    * identify reactive intermediates
    * write Bodenstein steady-state approximation for a reactive intermediate
    * eliminate concentrations of reactive intermediates from mechanistic rate expressions using the Bodenstein steady-state approximation
    * define the minimum number of apparent rate coefficients in a mechanistic rate expression
    * generate limiting forms of mechanistic rate expressions

## Prepare {.ch}

* Read Sections 4.1 - 4.3 and 4.6 and Example 4.8.1 from Chapter 4 of REB, The Book
* Watch the Class 4 Preparation Video
